messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failure occurs because SubLine.intersection computes the intersection point on the infinite supporting lines and then unconditionally projects that point into each sub-line’s 1D subspace, without checking whether the intersection actually exists.

Step-by-step:
- The test constructs two 3D segments:
  - sub1: from (1, 1, 1) to (1.5, 1, 1)
  - sub2: from (2, 3, 0) to (2, 3, 0.5)
  These underlying lines do not intersect (they are skew), so there is no intersection point.
- In org.apache.commons.math3.geometry.euclidean.threed.SubLine.intersection(SubLine, boolean):
  - It computes the intersection on the infinite lines:
    Vector3D v1D = line.intersection(subLine.line);  // line is sub1’s underlying Line
  - Line.intersection(Line) returns null when the lines do not intersect:
    return line.contains(closest) ? closest : null;
  - The code then immediately uses v1D:
    Location loc1 = remainingRegion.checkPoint(line.toSubSpace(v1D));
    Location loc2 = subLine.remainingRegion.checkPoint(subLine.line.toSubSpace(v1D));
- Since v1D is null, calling line.toSubSpace(v1D) triggers a NullPointerException. The toSubSpace method expects a non-null Vector and casts it to Vector3D before computing the abscissa:
  public Vector1D toSubSpace(final Vector<Euclidean3D> point) {
      return new Vector1D(getAbscissa((Vector3D) point));
  }
- This matches the bug report: NPE when calling SubLine.intersection() with non-intersecting lines; the NPE arises in Line.toSubSpace due to a null intersection point.
- The same pattern exists in the 2D implementation:
  org.apache.commons.math3.geometry.euclidean.twod.SubLine.intersection(SubLine, boolean) also computes v2D and then calls line.toSubSpace(v2D) without checking for null, leading to the same NPE when lines do not intersect.

Root cause:
- Missing null check after computing the intersection of the underlying infinite lines. If the intersection is null, the method should immediately return null instead of projecting a null point into subspace.

Expected fix:
- In both the 3D and 2D SubLine.intersection methods, add a guard:
  - If the intersection point (v1D/v2D) is null, return null immediately.
  - Otherwise proceed to check the point against the remaining regions (and includeEndPoints logic).

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
